title: Plane local testing of multiplicity codes via algebraic plane characterization

standard_prerequisites.name: Classical Grobner basis theory, Combinatorial Nullstellensatz with multiplicity [3], Lucas theorem, and imported Reed-Muller local tester [12]
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Exact author imported statements, definitions and their source-local explanations are retained. All local representing-polynomial, coefficient-isolation, degree and plane-sampling proofs retained; no recursive reconstruction of cited background results.

core_obligations: Represent arbitrary multiplicity tables modulo the multiplicity vanishing ideal using the author basis.
Isolate a noncanceling maximal coefficient after plane restriction and quotient reduction.
Choose a degree-sensitive exponent partition using Lucas theorem and its complete author digit argument.
Prove the plane test characterizes the code and convert that into the quantitative main plane tester using the full RM-to-MRM transfer context.
difficulty_reason: Combines Grobner quotient representatives with a specially ordered maximal basis term, noncancellation after a multivariate plane expansion, and a Lucas-digit partition. The characterization and its quantitative tester application form one main proof package, not separate support items.
